media.title: S.S. Champlain at Pier 57 — cabin-class salon, 1932
media.description: Cabin-class Salon de Thé aboard the French Line S.S. Champlain while associated with Pier 57 on the North River in 1932. The photograph documents the passenger-liner setting connected with the historical pier; it does not show the pier building or establish Kaper’s presence.
media.altText: Black-and-white photograph of the spacious cabin-class Salon de Thé aboard the S.S. Champlain, furnished with armchairs and small tables.
media.publicCaption: Cabin-class Salon de Thé aboard the French Line S.S. Champlain at Pier 57, North River, 1932.
media.publicCreditLine: Byron Company / Museum of the City of New York. 93.1.1.11445.
media.rightsNote: Copyright status has not been independently determined. The Museum of the City of New York describes conditions for non-commercial use of low-resolution images from its Collections Portal and notes that users must clear any copyright held by others. Its guidance requests a creator credit, accession number and link to the object record. The museum’s 2017 reproduction FAQ lists Byron Company among collections for which the museum can license images; it does not grant individual permission for this reproduction. The 1094 × 840 local image is used for scholarly illustration of the passenger-liner context associated with Pier 57; the museum’s description of low resolution does not specify a pixel threshold for this image.

places.authorizedName: French Line Pier 57, North River, foot of West 15th Street, Manhattan, New York
places.publicNote: Approximate arrival site for Kaper and Eleonora’s 1934 Atlantic crossing from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain. In this period the French Line (Compagnie Générale Transatlantique) used Pier 57 on the North River, at the foot of West 15th Street; the pier is inferred from the line’s documented berth rather than named in the passenger manifest. The record establishes arrival at New York but not processing at Ellis Island.
